newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian commerce minister denies labour abuses.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian commerce minister denies labour abuses.

text.p: Commerce Minister Cham Prasidh has criticised rights groups for opposing trade benefits for Cambodia and denied allegations that labour abuses are rife in the Southeast Asian nation.

Recent reports of child labour abuses were "weird prejudgements (based on) an obvious unawareness of the tragic circumstances the Cambodian people have gone through during the last two decades," Cham Prasidh wrote in a statement dated November 1 but released on Tuesday.
"One should question the concept which advocates all modern human rights need to be 100 percent implemented by disregarding the Cambodian context," the statement said.
Last week, the Asian-American Free Labor Institute (AAFLI) released a report alleging an increase in hazardous child labour practices in Cambodia.

In addition, the AFL-CIO, the largest American labour union, said alleged widespread labour abuses had prompted it to oppose the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) trade benefits for Cambodia. AAFLI is affiliated with the AFL-CIO.

A representative of AAFLI said escalating incidents of child labour, forced labour, poor working conditions and a lack of trade unions meant Cambodia did not meet the labour standards required for GSP status, which Cambodia applied for in October.
Cambodia is currently in the 30-day review period for GSP, a trade benefit that gives developing countries duty-free status on many exports to the U.S.
Cham Prasidh stated that he hopes to achieve GSP status for Cambodia by the end of the year despite the allegations, which he maintained were groundless.
